name: Kyriakos Mitsotakis
role: Prime Minister of Greece (since 2019); leader of New Democracy (since 2016)
summary: Mitsotakis is a centre-right, pro-European, market-friendly leader who combines liberal social reforms (same-sex marriage) with a tough line on irregular migration. He is firmly pro-NATO and pro-EU, backs Ukraine, supports a two-state settlement for Israel and Palestine and a bizonal federation for Cyprus, and has moved from cautious to open on gas extraction and nuclear power.

booksNotUsed.reason: Greek prime minister; no US congressional record.

public-ownership.rationale: He reported that his government moved to spur privatisation, cut taxes and open markets within its first three months.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The Mitsotakis government's bill legalising same-sex civil marriage and adoption passed parliament 176-76 in February 2024.

nation-first.rationale: He argues that multilateralism must be reinvigorated and that the world must act through international cooperation.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: He called the situation an acute climate crisis and committed to close all lignite plants early and pass a climate law, while keeping gas as a transitional fuel.

expand-nuclear.rationale: He announced Greece is 'turning the page' to explore small modular reactors, calling Europe's retreat from nuclear a strategic mistake, without yet committing to build.

conscription.rationale: A defence council he chaired raised compulsory military service from nine to twelve months, and he said the government was considering conscription from age 18.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: He said Greece is advancing exploration and potential exploitation of its offshore gas reserves with US partners and keeps gas as a bridge fuel.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: He calls the EU the most successful multilateral project and urges joint European borrowing for defence and a stronger EU role in its own defence.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: He said Greece is deepening its alliances and is firmly anchored in the EU, and he wants the EU mutual-assistance clause made operational.

collective-defense.rationale: He called for making Article 42.7, the EU mutual-assistance clause, truly operational, which treats an armed attack on one member as one on all.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: He proposed a single six-year presidential term because a second term risks politicising the office and undermining its non-partisan character.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: He praised the US founders for inserting checks and balances against democratic excess and called insulating decisions from the emotions of the moment a core preoccupation of democracy.

national-law-over-international.rationale: He said the only framework for resolving Greece's disputes with neighbours is international law and good neighbourly relations, and stressed respect for the rule of law over war.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: He said Greece is strengthening deterrence and deepening its alliances, and is anchored in the EU, so it is not staying out of blocs.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: He told Congress his parliament ratified the new US-Greece Mutual Defense and Cooperation Agreement, praised Souda Bay as the largest eastern Mediterranean naval base, and said it shows the enduring partnership.

state-laws-apply-online.rationale: He said digital technology is no different from any industry that must operate under health and safety regulation, and threatened harsher regulatory responses against platforms.

civil-marriage.rationale: The 2024 law he drove extended civil marriage to same-sex couples, passing 176-76.

turn-back-illegal-migrants.rationale: The government suspended asylum processing for sea arrivals from North Africa, ordered detention of illegal entrants and sought coast-guard cooperation to turn boats back.

notes: Themes searched: migration and asylum, same-sex marriage, energy and nuclear, defence and conscription, Ukraine, Cyprus and Turkey, EU and sovereignty, climate, technology regulation, US defence agreement, private universities, labour law (13-hour day), church-state relations and constitutional revision, assisted dying. The record available in the sources gives words or actions on only a limited set of the statements; the rest are left null. Greek-language sources were not searched.
